page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the n1 server family. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is configured with 30.0 GB of system memory, yielding 3.75 GB of RAM per core. It does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPU accelerators, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results place this instance primarily in the lower tiers for raw computational throughput. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests via stress-ng and Geekbench register in the weak to poor categories. However, memory subsystem performance is more balanced, with large-block read and write memory bandwidth tests, as well as the Passmark memory score, achieving average ratings. Ray tracing benchmarks also reach average performance levels, while text processing and compression tasks show poor throughput.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation and balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio, the n1-standard-8 offers a predictable resource profile for legacy workloads. While it lacks the high-frequency compute power of newer generations, its qualitative cost efficiency lies in hosting stable, non-burstable applications that require a steady memory footprint without demanding peak CPU performance. This server is suited for general-purpose workloads such as moderate web serving, basic database operations, and lightweight background processing tasks.
description: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-8 is an x86_64 general-purpose virtual machine featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs and 30.0 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz. Built on 4 physical cores with hyper-threading, it provides a balanced memory-to-core ratio of 3.75 GB per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks indicate weak single-core and multi-core CPU capabilities, alongside poor compression speeds. However, it maintains average performance in large-block memory bandwidth and ray tracing tasks. Lacking high-performance compute or fast local NVMe drives, the n1-standard-8 is best suited for stable, non-burstable general-purpose workloads, including moderate web serving, basic database operations, and lightweight background processing where predictable resource allocation is prioritized over raw processing speed.
